facts.blocked_reason: Admission is cleared and is no longer what blocks this row. All three journey identities hold an active sarah_voice_cohort:alpha_v1 row, and all three are admitted to NIP-29 group openagents-public by kind-9000 records the deployed authority config folds. Membership resolution is proven end to end: POST /api/sarah/livekit/room/join answers community_room_not_active (404) for each identity rather than community_membership_required (403). A moderator is reachable too: the access resolver derives isGroupAdmin solely from the authority config adminPubkeys, and Cloud Run revision openagents-monolith-00374-h4p adds an owned admin pubkey beside the existing one. What blocks the row now is the packaged client. rc29 exposes Join room, Summon Sarah, Talk to Sarah and Stop only as GPUI on_click closures in crates/agent_ui/src/omega_public_channel_view.rs. They are not registered GPUI actions, no keymap binding reaches them, the omega CLI flags target the agent-thread composer, the zed URL scheme has no route for them, omega-effectd is a private stdio pipe between the app and its own child process, and omega-device-bridge is an authenticated read-only mirror that refuses every command frame by design. So there is no unattended driver for the five controls this journey needs, and no packaged desktop reached a room join. Driving the HTTP routes directly instead would not be a packaged-desktop participant and is refused as evidence for this row.

facts.note: This receipt records what was actually observed for one Sarah LiveKit release-gate row on Omega v0.2.0-rc29. It never promotes source tests, configuration, deployment-lifecycle receipts, or a headless harness run into an installed packaged-candidate observation.

observed.headless_subscriber_fanout_composition: one owner participant plus one headless secondary subscriber
observed.packaged_desktop_profile_isolation_route: HOME and --user-data-dir co-located at <root>/Library/Application Support/Omega RC, which makes the rc29 provisioning root and registry root coincide

refused_claims: A subscriberFanoutCount of 2 headless subscribers is NOT a three-desktop journey and is not reported as one.
Passing server-side floor-authority unit tests in apps/openagents.com/workers/api are source evidence and cannot promote an installed-candidate row.
Three launched packaged desktops are NOT three authenticated room participants. Instance count is not admission, and this row still records authenticated_room_joins 0.
A cleared admission is NOT a journey. Every identity being admitted removes a precondition; it does not observe a single one of the nine required facts.
Driving /api/sarah/livekit/room/* directly with an identity's bearer is NOT a packaged-desktop participant, however authentic the identity. This row requires the client, not the contract.

The rc29 candidate does NOT carry the --user-data-dir identity fix. Omega ba6cc833b1 landed after the rc29 source c7ecf769e8, so isolated profiles authenticate on this candidate only through the co-located HOME route recorded above, not through the fix.

facts.unblocks_when: Three authenticated packaged Omega v0.2.0-rc29 desktops join one community room, summon Sarah, transfer the server-issued floor between two distinct members, all hear the shared answer, a moderator stops Sarah, and a non-floor participant, a stale grant, a replay, and a removed member are each refused. Admission no longer blocks step one. Two things do. First, the five community-room controls need a driver: either a human clicking them, or an unattended path that does not exist today. The only mechanism found is macOS Accessibility automation after opting each instance into ZED_EXPERIMENTAL_A11Y=1, which is undocumented, off by default, and named experimental; treat a run that needs it as a disclosed environment deviation. Second, the removed-member and stale-grant refusals need the serving image to carry openagents de475872af, which gives member_removed and membership_changed their first production emitter. That is a normal source deploy, not a credential.
